subject: history_social
passage: The rubber tree of Central America yields a milky latex that, on its own, dries into a brittle, crumbly solid. Yet peoples of ancient Mesoamerica were making useful rubber at least 3,000 years before vulcanization was patented in the 1840s. Chemists who studied ancient rubber artifacts and Spanish accounts worked out the method: the latex was mixed with juice squeezed from the stems of a morning glory vine, whose sulfur compounds linked the rubber molecules into a stretchy, durable network. More striking, the proportions were not fixed. Experiments reproducing the technique show that different ratios of latex to juice yield different qualities: more bounce for the solid balls used in ritual games, more toughness for sandal soles. The makers, it seems, were tailoring the recipe to the product.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Spanish writers of the 1500s were the first to describe how Mesoamerican peoples produced rubber.
choices.B: The rubber of ancient Mesoamerica was less durable than modern rubber because it was made without vulcanization.
choices.C: Latex from the rubber tree of Central America becomes stretchy and durable as soon as it dries.
choices.D: Mesoamerican peoples not only made rubber long before modern methods existed but adjusted the recipe to suit different uses.

explanation.why: The text makes two linked points: Mesoamerican peoples made rubber "at least 3,000 years before" vulcanization, and, "more striking," they varied the proportions of latex and vine juice to get bounce or toughness as needed. The last sentence sums up: "The makers ... were tailoring the recipe to the product." The main idea must include both the early date and the tailoring.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The Spanish accounts are one source the chemists used; the text does not say they were the first description, and this is a detail in any case.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares the durability of ancient and modern rubber; it describes the ancient rubber as "stretchy, durable."
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the first sentence, which says untreated latex dries into "a brittle, crumbly solid."
explanation.D: Correct. This covers the early date and the central point that the recipe was adjusted for different products.
